smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Divisibility argument
smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let the number be $\overline{ABC}$ with digit sum $s=A+B+C$. Then $s\mid100A+10B+C-s=99A+9B$, so $s\mid9(11A+B)$. Since the number is not a multiple of $3$, $s$ is not either, so $s\mid11A+B$. Take $A=9$ and test $B$ downward: $B=9,8,\ldots$ fail until $B=3$: $11A+B=102=2\cdot3\cdot17$ and $s=17$ works with $C=17-9-3=5$. The number $935=17\cdot55$ is not a multiple of $3$.

**Answer: 935**

smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Direct check
smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
Checking the three-digit numbers downward from $999$ by computer, the first number that is not a multiple of $3$ yet divisible by its digit sum is $935$ ($9+3+5=17$, $935=17\cdot55$).

**Answer: 935**

smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Inclusion-exclusion
smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
Only the letters $S,A,O,R$ appear in both names, so only they can coincide. The number of renamings with at least one of these fixed is, by inclusion-exclusion, $\binom41 7!-\binom42 6!+\binom43 5!-\binom44 4!=20160-4320+480-24=16296$. Subtracting from $8!=40320$: $40320-16296=24024$.

**Answer: 24024**

smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: AM-GM then rearrangement
smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
The three column products multiply to $9!=362880$, so their sum is smallest when they are as close to $\sqrt[3]{9!}\approx71$ as possible: the columns $\{2,5,7\},\{1,8,9\},\{3,4,6\}$ give products $70,72,72$, so $A=214$ is minimal. To maximize $B$ we want the row products as unequal as possible, so put the largest number of each column in one row, the middle ones in a second row and the smallest in the third: $9\cdot7\cdot6+8\cdot5\cdot4+1\cdot2\cdot3=378+160+6=544$.

**Answer: 544**

smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: Computer check
smt-2024-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
Brute force over all $9!$ grids gives minimum $A=214$ and, among those grids, maximum $B=544$.

**Answer: 544**
